SMTO-EXE-0266 — A workflow step couldn't run because what it depends on isn't ready

GUID: 58f67799-6dde-5422-baaa-8a87a7100882
Slug: recipe-precondition-failed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: recipes

What happened

  • A workflow step needed a result from an earlier step, or had to match exactly what was set up, and didn't. An earlier step may have failed. SMTO blocked the change and kept the steps that already finished.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the run's conversation and find the first step that failed or shows no result. Later steps only run after the steps before them succeed and give them what they need.
  2. Fix what that step needed, for example make sure the file, folder or account it uses exists, then ask SMTO in the conversation to continue. Once the earlier step succeeds, the blocked step can use its result.
  3. If the items the workflow works on have changed since it was saved, save your request again with Save to workflow so it looks them up fresh. An older workflow can point to items that no longer exist.
  4. Before starting the whole workflow over, check what the finished steps already changed. A full rerun could repeat those changes.

What success looks like

  • The blocked step runs and the remaining steps finish in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the workflow's name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't repeat a step when you aren't sure whether it already made its change.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The recorded-workflow guard blocked a step because a prerequisite step's result is unavailable, a short-lived target was saved as a fixed value, a previous step failed, or the requested write does not match any pending step's reviewed arguments.

What this means

  • A prerequisite receipt or result pointer is unavailable, an ephemeral target was retained as a literal, a prior step failed, or a requested mutation does not match a pending eligible step's exact reviewed arguments. Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.

Why this can happen

  • A prerequisite receipt or result pointer is unavailable, an ephemeral target was retained as a literal, a prior step failed, or a requested mutation does not match a pending eligible step's exact reviewed arguments.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect prerequisite step states, fresh bindings and the proposed arguments against the pinned workflow.

How to fix it

  • Inspect recipe_steps in the task state and the guard, _results and render paths in src/agent_runtime/recipes/runtime.py and bindings.py. Make sure prerequisite steps completed with successful results, short-lived fields (element_ref, session_id and similar) use $step bindings, and write arguments exactly match the reviewed template; fix the failed prerequisite or re-save the workflow, and never re-run completed writes.
  • Obtain the missing current evidence or correct the invocation to the reviewed step; preserve completed steps and existing approvals.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the workflow and its current run evidence before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • Current prerequisite evidence resolves and the next pending step matches the reviewed arguments and effect.

What not to do

  • Never repeat a write whose effect remains unknown.

Technical notes

  • Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
